name: atlas
description: MarineSensitivity Atlas: scores, species, places and reports for U.S. marine areas.

pinReasons._: package.json is JSON and cannot carry a real comment, so these entries ARE the inline reason (atlas-refs/'calcofi explore review.md' §11 lesson 10). Full evidence and the wiring each pin depends on: docs/spikes/S1.md, S2.md, S4.md. tests/pins.test.ts fails if a range here drifts from its verdict line.
pinReasons.d3-hierarchy: atlas-3 step 2b: EXACT 3.1.2 (not from a dedicated spike -- pinned for the same reason as the others: a dependency that must stay LAZY should not silently change behavior on `npm install` from an unreviewed bump). Treemap.svelte reaches it ONLY through a dynamic import() -- it must never enter index.html's static graph (scripts/size-budget-core.mjs's FORBIDDEN_LAZY_MARKERS already lists "treemap"; tests/fixtures/size-budget-static-treemap/ is the committed red fixture proving a static import of it fails the checker). Only `hierarchy()`/`.sum()` are used, to build the tree and roll up values -- the actual squarified layout math is this repo's own pure function (src/lib/ui/treemapLayout.ts), unit-tested independently of d3.
pinReasons.@duckdb/duckdb-wasm: EXACT 1.32.0, no caret (S1). npm 'latest' (1.33.1-dev57.0) creates OPFS files and never writes to them: the reopen after a reload throws 'Catalog Error: Table with name t does not exist!' on chromium AND firefox. 1.33.1-dev64.0 ('next') also passes but is a moving dist-tag on a dev build. A caret would admit a future stable 1.33.x, which is the line the write bug lives in and which nobody has tested. Bumping this means re-running spikes/1/e2e/persistence.spec.js; dev57 must stay red.
pinReasons.maplibre-gl: ^6.10.0 (S2). NOT the subplan's '^5.24' fallback: GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579 is critical (CVSS 10.0, XSS sanitizer bypass), vulnerable range <=6.4.0, first patched 6.4.1 — all 35 published 5.x releases are inside it and none is or will be patched. 6.10.0 starts under Vite 8 and renders 10 zones-line vector features with zero worker/shared 404s in all four dev/build x optimizeDeps.exclude cells (spikes/2's committed VECTOR GATE); first paint clears the 2.5s budget on 6.10 in 18 of 18 cold standalone runs (firstDataFrame medians 740.3ms and 662.2ms over two N=9 samples), though the same gate is flaky inside the parallel suite (2 of 6 runs over budget: titiler latency + contention) and has never run on CI — atlas-8 runs it alone. Works ONLY with named imports (6.x has no default export: a default import is a hard Rolldown [MISSING_EXPORT] build failure) and the worker wired as `maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?worker&url` + setWorkerUrl(). Plain '?url' emits the worker without its 514 KB shared chunk, which then 404s: rasters still paint, vector tiles silently never parse.
pinReasons.shpjs: EXACT 6.2.0 (S4), the version measured. Correctness here is the bundled proj4 reprojection from a shapefile's .prj: 0.000000 m from the GDAL/PROJ ground truth on the UTM fixture. It is also the one parser that silently returns raw metres when the .prj is missing (no warning, no error), so atlas-6's CRS gate is written against this exact behaviour. 46.7 KB gzip — must stay a dynamic import. Bumping means re-running spikes/4/e2e/correctness.spec.ts.
pinReasons.@tmcw/togeojson: EXACT 7.1.2 (S4), the version measured for KML (3.8 KB gzip lazy). GPX shares the package but was NOT exercised by any fixture — add one before advertising GPX.
pinReasons.flatgeobuf: EXACT 4.4.0 (S4), the version measured. Fastest parser here (2.3 ms for 40k vertices, 11.4 KB gzip) and it reports the source CRS in the header but does NOT reproject: atlas-6's normalizer must, and that division of labour is version-specific behaviour worth pinning.
pinReasons.pmtiles: ^4.5.0 (atlas-map). The pmtiles:// protocol src/lib/map/map.ts registers with maplibre's addProtocol, and the version spike S2's harness measured alongside maplibre-gl 6.10 (spikes/2/package.json). Caret, not exact: it is not one of S2's verdict pins -- S2 pinned only maplibre-gl -- and its own failure mode (a range read that returns the wrong bytes) is caught loudly by e2e/map.spec.ts's rendered-vector-feature assertion against a real archive, not silently. It is part of the 288 KB maplibre+pmtiles critical-path measurement D13's 450 KB budget was set from, so a bump means re-reading `npm run size-budget`.
pinReasons.terra-draw: EXACT 1.35.0 (atlas-6 step 2). No dedicated spike (not one of S1/S2/S4, so tests/pins.test.ts's spike-verdict gate does not cover this pair) -- pinned anyway for the same reason every lazy dependency here is: a version bump changing mode behaviour must be a reviewed diff, not a silent `npm install`. Reached only through `src/places/draw.ts`'s dynamic `import()`; `tests/places/lazyImports.test.ts` is this pair's own version of `tests/geo/upload/lazyImports.test.ts`.
pinReasons.terra-draw-maplibre-gl-adapter: EXACT 1.4.1, matching terra-draw's own pin above (peerDependencies: `terra-draw@^1.0.0`, `maplibre-gl@>=4` -- both satisfied by this repo's pins). Its own version numbering lags terra-draw's (1.x vs 1.35.x): they are published from separate packages, not a lockstep monorepo, so pin both explicitly rather than assume a caret keeps them compatible.
pinReasons.qrcode-generator: ^1.5.2 (atlas-7 step 2/3). The report header's permalink QR -- reached ONLY through `src/report/qr.ts`'s dynamic `import()`, never a static import, so it never enters `report.html`'s own critical-path budget. No dedicated spike; caret is fine because the module's whole surface used here is `qrcode(typeNumber, errorCorrectionLevel)` + `.make()`/`.createSvgTag()`, a stable API this package has not broken across 1.x.
pinReasons.fflate: ^0.8.3 (atlas-7 step 3). The data-package ZIP exporter -- reached ONLY through `src/report/exportZip.ts`'s dynamic `import()`. Chosen over JSZip for size (this package's whole `zip`/`strToU8` surface is a few KB gzip); caret is fine, no format-sensitive behaviour pinned.
pinReasons.docx: ^9.7.1 (atlas-7 step 3, master plan D9: Word yes, no reference template so coded styles). The `.docx` exporter -- reached ONLY through `src/report/exportDocx.ts`'s dynamic `import()`. Caret: this repo only uses the documented `Document`/`Paragraph`/`Table`/`ImageRun` builder API, not template-fidelity behaviour a patch bump would change.
